messages:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT: Dedicated pool Dedicated-GPU-ACME-01 in us-west-2 reporting GPU exhaustion and increasing 5xxs for tenant acme-corp. Paging Maya (primary).
Maya (oncall): ack. pulling telemetry.
Alex (oncall): jumping in. what's current pool size and queue?
Maya (oncall): pool = 6 nodes, all 8 GPUs each, but 6 nodes are saturated. queue depth ~200, error spikes to 20/s. p95 > 3s.
Raj (dedicated-ops): confirmed. Their workload is pinned to acme-large-bert (single-shard, high VRAM). Autoscaler did not trigger because tenant-level auto-burst = disabled and the pool is at hard shard limit.
Linda (eng-platform): autoscaler logs show scale decisions blocked by tenant isolation policy. We have two levered paths: enable cross-tenant burst, or add dedicated nodes. Enabling cross-tenant burst requires acct-exec + legal signoff per contract.
Tim (support): ACME reported timeouts at 10:18p PT, they're escalating internally. CSM already notified customer.
Oliver (CSM): ACME wants 'no functional regression' and minimal interruption. They asked if we can spin up extra nodes or shift some traffic gracefully.
Maya (oncall): triage options:
- (1) Add dedicated nodes into their pool (estimated 15-22m to ready)
- (2) Enable temporary cross-tenant burst to shared-burst-usw2 (fast, may violate isolation terms if not approved)
- (3) Route ACME inference to a quantized model variant we host in shared pool (lower cost/less VRAM) but possible quality delta.
Raj (dedicated-ops): infra can spin 2 nodes fast (~12m) or 4 nodes in ~20m. Quota available: spare_gpu_quota=6 for acme-corp.
Alex (oncall): do we have a quantized fallback for acme-large-bert available in shared pool?
Linda (eng-platform): we have acme-large-bert-q4 in shared-burst-usw2 but customer pinned their endpoint to the exact model hash that doesn't have q4. We can create a routing override to swap model variant during emergency. That needs CSM + acct-exec approval to change the pinned model temporarily.
Carla (acct-exec): I can approve emergency cross-pool routing if legal signs off. I'll also note the emergency-burst fees to billing.
Priya (legal): quick read: emergency routing allowed under SOW but must be timeboxed and logged. I approve for up to 1.5 hours if CSM confirms ACME consent or we have emergency-burst contractual clause invoked.
Oliver (CSM): I messaged ACME PM: "We can route to a lower-VRAM quantized variant in shared pool or enable emergency burst. Which preferred?" They replied: "Prefer minimal user-visible change. If quantized model is indistinguishable, do that; otherwise burst."
Maya (oncall): fine. Plan: 1) apply model-variant override to quantized fallback in shared pool for read traffic; 2) simultaneously kick off adding 3 dedicated nodes; 3) enable temporary cross-pool routing only for inference and only while queue > 10.
Raj (dedicated-ops): executing node scale now:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool Dedicated-GPU-ACME-01 --add-nodes 3 --type p4dn --region us-west-2
```
deploy-bot: scale job queued (job-id: jb-904112). est ready 18m.
Alex (oncall): applying model override for tenant:
```
redwoodctl model route set --tenant acme-corp --endpoint /v1/inference --model acme-large-bert-q4 --target shared-burst-usw2 --ttl 1h --note "emergency quantized fallback"
```
Maya (oncall): override applied. Monitor shows immediate drop in queue depth to 60 and lowered memory footprints on hosts. Latency + quality sampling will be monitored.
Tim (support): ACME confirms they see fewer timeouts. They ran a quick smoke and said outputs look 'mostly same' for 95% of requests. Some longer prompts show slightly different truncation behavior.
Priya (legal): make sure we capture consent timeline in ACME exchange. Oliver, please paste consent in the ticket.
Oliver (CSM): pasted consent snapshot into the customer record and notified finance about potential emergency charges.
Raj (dedicated-ops): dedicated nodes are joining: nd-acme-11, nd-acme-12, nd-acme-13. Registration complete, warming caches.
Maya (oncall): once nodes healthy, we'll drain the shared override.
Alex (oncall): health checks green. Initiating rollback of the model-route override:
```
redwoodctl model route delete --tenant acme-corp --endpoint /v1/inference --note "rollback after dedicated nodes ready"
```
Maya (oncall): rollback done. Traffic flows back to dedicated pool. Current queue 8, p95 ~650ms, errors -> 0.
Carla (acct-exec): logged emergency-burst incident and estimated cost for the quantized shared usage + new nodes ~ $4k. Sending invoice notice to ACME finance.
Priya (legal): marking incident as within emergency scope; no breach.
Maya (oncall): post-incident actions:
- Add explicit contractual toggle for auto-burst for enterprise tenants (Carla + Priya)
- Add runbook to prefer quantized fallback with CSM consent (Linda + Alex)
- Tune autoscaler to detect pinned high-VRAM model patterns (Raj)
- Telemetry: add alert for pool VRAM saturation (Maya)
Raj (dedicated-ops): postmortem owner assigned: Raj. I'll gather runbook logs, scale timelines, and infra traces.
Maya (oncall): closing thread - service restored. :white_check_mark: Will attach logs and the redwoodctl commands used to the postmortem ticket.
